project.name: Fakkerni
project.description: Fakkerni is an Arabic-first native Android reminder app with a SwiftUI companion for iPhone and iPad. It supports reviewed voice or typed reminder capture, local contacts, and locally scheduled alerts, with separate reminder storage on each platform. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Start With the Product
tour.description: Fakkerni turns Arabic-first voice capture into a reminder that the user reviews and approves before scheduling. Read the overview and product guide to understand the two native applications, optional AI, local contacts and separate on-device reminder stores. This approval boundary explains the design choices throughout the tour.

tour.title: Enter Both Native Apps
tour.description: The product in Step 1 has separate Android and SwiftUI entry points. MainActivity presents reminder lists and navigation, while FakkerniApp starts the iOS onboarding and assistant experience and routes notification responses. AppModel owns the iOS state that connects those screens to reminders and settings.
tour.languageLesson: SwiftUI declares screens from state, and observable state changes drive rendering; Android activities instead manage platform lifecycle callbacks and native view objects.

tour.title: Learn the Reminder Contract
tour.description: Before following the entry points into capture, learn the difference between an editable draft and a stored reminder. The Android model and VoiceDraft validator mirror the iOS core's normalized fields and strict future wall-clock checks. These contracts keep incomplete or ambiguous AI output available for review instead of treating it as an approved event.

tour.title: Capture and Cancel Voice
tour.description: With the draft contract established, follow how the assistant obtains a recording. Android VoiceInput and iOS VoiceRecorder manage microphone permission, recording and asynchronous work before handing a draft to review. Cancellation and temporary recording cleanup make the capture lifecycle part of application behavior, rather than merely a microphone button.

tour.title: Turn Audio Into Drafts
tour.description: The recording flow from Step 4 calls the selected provider through native HTTP clients. Android's historically named OpenAiClient and iOS AIClient support Groq, OpenAI and Gemini, validate structured responses and preserve successful transcripts when separate extraction fails. That fallback returns useful text to the review flow introduced by the reminder contract.

tour.title: Connect One Active Provider
tour.description: The clients in Step 5 depend on an explicitly configured provider connection. Android verifies credentials and stores separate encrypted provider keys, while iOS settings provide an app-owned return action from the provider browser and require an entered, verified API key before activation. More than one connection can be stored, but voice requests use one active provider.

tour.title: Keep Approval Explicit
tour.description: The provider connection enables draft generation but does not authorize saving. AddReminderActivity and ReminderScreens let the user inspect and edit proposed content, validate the event time and explicitly approve a reminder; manual capture reaches the same boundary without an AI request. The iOS surface guide explains how this review fits the assistant-first interface.

tour.title: Resolve Contacts Locally
tour.description: A reviewed draft may include a person's name or phone number, so the editor from Step 7 needs local contact resolution. Android separates address-book access from name matching, while the iOS core handles Arabic/English aliases and conservative cross-script matching. The address book stays local, and a reminder's call action leads to the system phone flow.

tour.title: Persist Approved Reminders
tour.description: Once the user approves the completed draft, each platform stores its own reminders locally. Android uses synchronized JSON access in SharedPreferences, while the iOS core provides atomic JSON persistence. AppModel coordinates iOS scheduling and saving, restoring previous alerts if persistence fails.

tour.title: Deliver Native Local Alerts
tour.description: The saved reminders from Step 9 drive platform-specific alert delivery, normally one hour before the event with a short fallback for nearby events. Android separates scheduling, notification presentation and rescheduling after system changes; iOS delegates delivery to native local notifications with selected sounds and optional call actions. The Android manifest registers the receivers and permissions that make that background behavior possible.

tour.title: Read the Visual Language
tour.description: After tracing reminder behavior, look at how both applications present it consistently. Android's shared UI and locale helpers combine with XML palette resources, while iOS Visuals supplies adaptive colors, Cairo typography, animated icons and the reactive orb. These are native presentation implementations supporting the same Arabic/English product identity.

tour.title: Prepare Shared Native Assets
tour.description: The visual and sound resources used in Step 11 are prepared by a small tooling layer. JavaScript scripts compile Morphicons frame data and adapt shared assets for iOS, including converting nine Android MP3 tones to CAF and invoking the Swift icon renderer. Native metadata declares the font, localization and privacy information packaged with the iOS app.
tour.languageLesson: The .mjs extension marks a Node.js ES module. Here JavaScript supports asset preparation, while the application interfaces and runtime behavior remain Java and Swift.

tour.title: Verify the Product Boundaries
tour.description: The tests connect the previous steps into checkable behavior: date validation, transcript fallback, provider isolation, approval and persistence. Swift core tests mock networking, iOS UI tests cover the provider browser return and review flow, and Android instrumentation exercises native behavior on disposable emulators. Reading these tests shows what is asserted; their presence alone does not establish that a current device or build run passed.

tour.title: Build and Package Both Apps
tour.description: Finish by connecting the verified behavior to the native build definitions. Gradle builds Android, while XcodeGen connects the iOS app and UI tests to the FakkerniCore package; the macOS workflow runs core tests and the iOS script. That script collects simulator results and packages an unsigned IPA, so signing and installation remain part of the documented distribution workflow.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions YAML uses triggers to select runs and sequential steps within jobs. The shell script holds the native build sequence, while the Swift package manifest defines the reusable core and its test target.
